verses.zh: 看哪，必有一王凭公义行政；必有首领藉公平掌权。
verses.en: Look, a king will promote fairness;[NOTE:1] officials will promote justice.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “will reign according to fairness.”
Heb “will rule according to justice.”

verses.zh: 必有一人像避风所和避暴雨的隐密处，又像河流在干旱之地，像大磐石的影子在疲乏之地。
verses.en: Each of them[NOTE:1] will be like a shelter from the windand a refuge from a rainstorm;like streams of water in a dry regionand like the shade of a large cliff in a parched land.
notes: Heb “a man,” but אִישׁ (ʾish) probably refers here to “each” of the officials mentioned in the previous verse.

verses.zh: 那能看的人，眼不再昏迷；能听的人，耳必得听闻。
verses.en: Eyes[NOTE:1] will no longer be blind[NOTE:2] and ears[NOTE:3] will be attentive.
notes: Heb “Eyes that see.”

The Hebrew text as vocalized reads literally “will not gaze,” but this is contradictory to the context. The verb form should be revocalized as תְּשֹׁעֶינָה (teshoʿenah) from שָׁעַע (shʿaʿa, “be blinded”); see Isa 6:10; 29:9.
Heb “ears that hear.”

verses.zh: 冒失人的心必明白知识；结巴人的舌必说话通快。
verses.en: The mind that acts rashly will possess discernment,[NOTE:1] and the tongue that stutters will speak with ease and clarity.
notes: Heb “the heart of rashness will understand knowledge”; cf. NAB “The flighty will become wise and capable.”

verses.zh: 愚顽人不再称为高明；吝啬人不再称为大方。
verses.en: A fool will no longer be called honorable;a deceiver will no longer be called principled.

verses.zh: 因为愚顽人必说愚顽话，心里想作罪孽，惯行亵渎的事，说错谬的话攻击耶和华，使饥饿的人无食可吃，使口渴的人无水可喝。
verses.en: For a fool speaks disgraceful things;[NOTE:1] his mind plans out sinful deeds.[NOTE:2] He commits godless deeds[NOTE:3] and says misleading things about the Lord;he gives the hungry nothing to satisfy their appetite[NOTE:4] and gives the thirsty nothing to drink.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “foolishness,” in a moral-ethical sense. See 9:17.
Heb “and his heart commits sin”; KJV, ASV “his heart will work iniquity”; NASB “inclines toward wickedness.”
Heb “in order to do [or “so that he does”] what is godless [or “defiled”].”
Heb “so that he leaves empty the appetite [or “desire”] of the hungry.”
Heb “and the drink of the thirsty he causes to fail.”

verses.zh: 吝啬人所用的法子是恶的；他图谋恶计，用谎言毁灭谦卑人；穷乏人讲公理的时候，他也是这样行。
verses.en: A deceiver’s methods are evil;[NOTE:1] he dreams up evil plans[NOTE:2] to ruin the poor with lies,even when the needy are in the right.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “as for a deceiver, his implements [or “weapons”] are evil.”
Or “he plans evil things”; NIV11 “they make up evil schemes.”
Heb “to ruin the poor with words of falsehood, even when the needy speak what is just.”

verses.zh: 高明人却谋高明事，在高明事上也必永存。
verses.en: An honorable man makes honorable plans;his honorable character gives him security.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he upon honorable things stands.”

verses.zh: 安逸的妇女啊，起来听我的声音！无虑的女子啊，侧耳听我的言语！
verses.en: You complacent[NOTE:1] women,get up and listen to me!You carefree[NOTE:2] daughters,pay attention to what I say!
notes: Or “self-assured”; NASB, NRSV “who are at ease.”
Or “self-confident”; NAB “overconfident.”

verses.zh: 无虑的女子啊，再过一年多，必受骚扰；因为无葡萄可摘，无果子（或译：禾稼）可收。
verses.en: In a year’s time[NOTE:1] you carefree ones will shake with fear,for the grape harvest[NOTE:2] will fail,and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
notes: Heb “days upon a year.”
Or perhaps, “olive.” See 24:13.

verses.zh: 安逸的妇女啊，要战兢；无虑的女子啊，要受骚扰。脱去衣服，赤着身体，腰束麻布。
verses.en: Tremble, you complacent ones!Shake with fear, you carefree ones!Strip off your clothes and expose yourselves—put sackcloth around your waists.[NOTE:1]
notes: The imperatival forms in v. 11 are problematic. The first (חִרְדוּ, khiredu, “tremble”) is masculine plural in form, though spoken to a feminine plural addressee (שַׁאֲנַנּוֹת, shaʾanannot, “complacent ones”). The four imperatival forms that follow (רְגָזָה, regazah, “shake with fear”; פְּשֹׁטָה, peshotah, “strip off your clothes”; עֹרָה, ʿorah, “expose yourselves”; and חֲגוֹרָה, khagorah, “put on”) all appear to be lengthened (so-called “emphatic”) masculine singular forms, even though they too appear to be spoken to a feminine plural addressee. GKC 131-32 §48.i suggests emending חִרְדוּ (khiredu) to חֲרָדָה (kharadah) and understanding all five imperatives as feminine plural “Aramaized” forms.

verses.zh: 她们必为美好的田地和多结果的葡萄树，捶胸哀哭。
verses.en: Mourn over the field,[NOTE:1] over the delightful fieldsand the fruitful vine.
notes: The Hebrew text has “over mourning breasts.” The reference to “breasts” would make sense in light of v. 11, which refers to the practice of women baring their breasts as a sign of sorrow (see J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 1:585). However, one expects the preposition עַל (ʿal) to introduce the source or reason for mourning (see vv. 12b-13a) and the participle סֹפְדִים (sofedim, “mourning”) seems odd modifying “breasts.” The translation above assumes a twofold emendation: (1) שָׁדַיִם (shadayim, “breasts”) is emended to [ם]שָׂדַי (saday[m], “field,” a term that also appears in Isa 56:9). The final mem (ם) would be enclitic in this case, not a plural indicator. (The Hebrew noun שָׂדֶה (sadeh, “field”) forms its plural with an וֹת- [-ot] ending). (2) The plural participle סֹפְדִים is emended to סְפֹדָה (sefodah), a lengthened imperatival form, meaning “mourn.” For an overview of various suggestions that have been made for this difficult line, see Oswalt, 586, n. 12).

verses.zh: 荆棘蒺藜必长在我百姓的地上，又长在欢乐的城中和一切快乐的房屋上。
verses.en: Mourn[NOTE:1] over the land of my people,which is overgrown with thorns and briers,and over all the once-happy houses[NOTE:2] in the city filled with revelry.[NOTE:3]
notes: “Mourn” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text vv. 12-13 are one long sentence.
Heb “indeed, over all the houses of joy.” It is not certain if this refers to individual homes or to places where parties and celebrations were held.
This same phrase is used in 22:2.

verses.zh: 因为宫殿必被撇下，多民的城必被离弃；山冈望楼永为洞穴，作野驴所喜乐的，为羊群的草场。
verses.en: For the fortress is neglected;the once-crowded[NOTE:1] city is abandoned.Hill[NOTE:2] and watchtowerare permanently uninhabited.[NOTE:3] Wild donkeys love to go there,and flocks graze there.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “noisy” (NAB, NIV, NCV).
Hebrew עֹפֶל (ʿofel), probably refers here to a specific area within the city of Jerusalem. See HALOT 861 s.v. II עֹפֶל.

The Hebrew text has בְעַד מְעָרוֹת (veʿad meʿarot). The force of בְעַד, which usually means “behind, through, round about,” or “for the benefit of,” is uncertain here. HALOT 616 s.v. *מְעָרָה takes מְעָרוֹת (meʿarot) as a homonym of “cave” and defines it here as “cleared field.” Despite these lexical problems, the general point of the statement seems clear—the city will be uninhabited.
Heb “the joy of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks.”

verses.zh: 等到圣灵从上浇灌我们，旷野就变为肥田，肥田看如树林。
verses.en: This desolation will continue[NOTE:1] until new life is poured out on us from heaven.[NOTE:2] Then the wilderness will become an orchard[NOTE:3]and the orchard will be considered a forest.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “The desolation will continue” refer to the previous context and have been added for smoothness.

Heb “until a spirit is emptied out on us from on high.” The words “this desolation will continue” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic purposes. The verb עָרָה (ʿarah), used here in the Niphal, normally means “lay bare, expose.” The term רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) is often understood here as a reference to the divine spirit (cf. 44:3 and NASB, NIV, CEV, NLT), but it appears here without an article (cf. NRSV “a spirit”), pronominal suffix, or a genitive (such as “of the Lord”). The translation assumes that it carries an impersonal nuance “vivacity, vigor” in this context.

The term כַּרְמֶל (karmel) may refer to fertile land, an orchard, a garden of vines, a plantation of trees, or fresh grain. The dictionaries may subdivide these meaning under homonyms (see BDB 502, NIDOTTE 718, HALOT 499, The Concise DCH, 183). The picture of transformation is clearer when it is understood that a מִדְבָּר (midbar, “wilderness”) is an area that does not receive enough rainfall to support trees.

The same statement appears in 29:17b, where, in conjunction with the preceding line, it appears to picture a reversal. Here it seems to depict supernatural growth. The desert will blossom into an orchard, and the trees of the orchard will multiply and grow tall, becoming a forest.

verses.zh: 那时，公平要居在旷野；公义要居在肥田。
verses.en: Justice will settle down in the wildernessand fairness will live in the orchard.[NOTE:1]
notes: This new era of divine blessing will also include a moral/ethical transformation, as justice and fairness fill the land and replace the social injustice so prevalent in Isaiah’s time.

verses.zh: 公义的果效必是平安；公义的效验必是平稳，直到永远。
verses.en: Fairness will produce peace[NOTE:1] and result in lasting security.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the product of fairness will be peace.”
Heb “and the work of fairness [will be] calmness and security forever.”

verses.zh: 我的百姓必住在平安的居所，安稳的住处，平静的安歇所。
verses.en: My people will live in peaceful settlements,in secure homes,and in safe, quiet places.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “in safe resting places”; NAB, NRSV “quiet resting places.”

verses.zh: （但要降冰雹打倒树林；城必全然拆平。）
verses.en: Even if the forest is destroyed[NOTE:1] and the city is annihilated,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and [?] when the forest descends.” The form וּבָרַד (uvarad) is often understood as an otherwise unattested denominative verb meaning “to hail” (HALOT 154 s.v. I ברד). In this case one might translate, “and it hails when the forest is destroyed” (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV). Perhaps the text alludes to a powerful wind and hail storm that knocks down limbs and trees. Some prefer to emend the form to וְיָרַד (veyarad), “and it descends,” which provides better, though not perfect, symmetry with the parallel line (cf. NAB). Perhaps וּבָרַד should be dismissed as dittographic. In this case the statement (“when the forest descends”) lacks a finite verb and seems incomplete, but perhaps it is subordinate to v. 20.
Heb “and in humiliation the city is laid low.”

verses.zh: 你们在各水边撒种、牧放牛驴的有福了！
verses.en: you will be blessed,you who plant seed by all the banks of the streams,[NOTE:1] you who let your ox and donkey graze.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “by all the waters.”

Heb “who set free the foot of the ox and donkey”; NIV “letting your cattle and donkeys range free.”sn This verse seems to anticipate a time when fertile land is available to cultivate and crops are so abundant that the farm animals can be allowed to graze freely.
